question: Can a causal, body-referenced release event (the ball leaving contact with the hand while ascending) replace the fixed 2.0 s wall-clock cutoff on development participants, and does the observed 200 ms after that event look like free flight in every participant/session, unlike the fixed cutoff (OW-REGIME-17)? Feasibility only: detection coverage, exclusions and post-event regime diagnostics; no forecasting comparison.
design_disclosure: the contact boundary and the ascending condition were chosen after inspecting four development trials (one per participant/session: ball-hand distance ~0.01-0.19 m while held, growing ~0.5 m per 0.1 s after release; an incoming pass and downward dribbles in the 2024 session). The boundary comes from ball geometry, not from any forecast error.

not_opened.P0004: its one permitted consultation was spent in OW-REGIME-19

ball_input: time axis, ball coordinates and frame indices come from OW-REGIME-17's load_trial (identical ball input to the fixed-cutoff diagnostics); hand keypoints come from wms.data.mlse_spl.load_spl_free_throw, whose ball array must equal load_trial's (NaN-aware) or the run blocks
ball_radius_derivation: r = circumference / (2*pi) * 0.0254 m (29.5 in men's size-7 ball); derived in code, not transcribed
contact_boundary_definition: contact_boundary_radii * r (one ball diameter): the nearest finite hand keypoint lies within this distance of the ball centre
sensitivity_role: event times at 1.5r and 3r are reported descriptively as shifts from the 2r event; they never choose the event
hand_keypoints: every keypoint named LEFT_* or RIGHT_* containing WRIST, THUMB, PINKY or FINGER; per sample only finite keypoints are used and at least one is required; keypoints absent in a schema stay absent (NaN), never imputed
event_rule: a sample is evaluable when the ball and >= 1 hand keypoint are finite; contact means the evaluable min ball-hand distance <= boundary. Scan evaluable samples in time order. A transition is an evaluable sample beyond the boundary whose immediately preceding evaluable sample was in contact. The release event is the FIRST transition with: time gap to the preceding evaluable sample <= 1.6 native frames, and ascending: the OLS vertical velocity over finite ball samples in [t_i - history_s, t_i] (>= 3 samples) is > 0. Only samples at or before t_i are used (causal).
excluded_transitions: transitions before the event that fail a condition are counted per trial by reason (time_gap, descending, direction_unknown when fewer than 3 finite ball samples) and never become the event. A ball never within the boundary (e.g. an incoming pass) produces no transition. A trial without an event is no_contact (never in contact) or no_ascending_release.
post_event_diagnostics: the time axis is shifted so the event sample lands exactly on the baseline cutoff (2.0 s); OW-REGIME-17's trial_diagnostics with its frozen config (regime17_config) then reports prefix eligibility under the unchanged baseline rule, native target availability, future-window fits (free-quadratic vertical acceleration, gravity/constant-velocity RMSE ratio), tracking tail and the noncausal ballistic-window heuristic. These are noncausal DIAGNOSTICS of the post-event interval, never labels or model inputs.
separation_persistence: descriptive: min ball-hand distance at the first evaluable sample >= 0.1 s after the event minus the distance at the event (noncausal check that the separation did not reverse)
comparison: per group, the fixed-cutoff future_fits and release_heuristic counts and the quantiles of the future-fit diagnostics (all trials and prefix-eligible) are copied from OW-REGIME-17's retained manifest beside the post-event values
examples: per participant/session, the trial whose event time is the lower median within the group (ties broken by path) is plotted: ball-hand distance and ball height against time since the event over [-0.6, +0.6] s, with the boundaries and the fixed 2.0 s cutoff marked
verification: verify-retained checks digests, replays the frozen config, rebuilds the summary from the per-trial rows, and with --data-root re-derives every per-trial row from the pinned data and requires exact equality
decision: counts, reasons and quantiles only; no thresholds on the outcome. Whether a forecasting task card (OW-EVENT-21) is frozen depends on the recorded coverage and post-event regime distributions
